transcript.text:
A freezer that keeps beeping is usually its door or high-temperature alarm, rather than the beep itself being the fault. The common causes are a door not sealing, something preventing it closing, or the freezer having warmed up after a door was left open or food was added. 1. Check both fridge and freezer doors close flush all the way round. Look for a packet, drawer or shelf stopping either door, and check the rubber seals for dirt, folds, gaps or damage. Clean and dry a dirty seal, then close the door firmly. If the alarm stops, it was a door/seal issue.
2. Check whether the freezer contents feel solidly frozen. If food is softening or there is a lot of thawing, keep the doors shut as much as possible and avoid adding warm food; the beeping is warning that it is too warm.
3. If it is cold and both doors seal properly but the alarm continues, a door switch, temperature sensor or control fault becomes more likely and would need diagnosis. Are both doors closing and sealing fully, and does the freezer feel properly cold or warmer than usual?
the bottom freezer drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night, a bag was sticking out. ive shut it now. ice cream is a bit soft round the edges but the rest is hard

The bag holding the freezer drawer out is very likely the cause. The beep will usually be a door/temperature alarm: warm air got in overnight, so the appliance may continue alarming until the freezer has pulled back down to temperature. Ice cream softening slightly at the edges fits that; the rest being hard is reassuring. 1. Keep the drawer fully closed and avoid opening it unnecessarily for the next few hours. Do not add warm food. The alarm should stop once it recovers; many models also need the alarm button pressed once to silence it after the cause has been corrected.
2. Check the drawer closes flush and that the rubber seal is clean, flat and not trapped by a bag or drawer edge. A gap would allow the alarm to return. If it is still beeping continuously after the drawer has remained properly shut and the food is fully firm again, the next possibilities are a seal/drawer-closing issue or, less commonly, a temperature sensor fault. Now the drawer is fully shut, does the beeping stop after a little while, or is it still beeping continuously?
its still beeping. the freezer temp number is flashing -9 and going down slowly

The flashing -9°C and its slow fall show the freezer is still recovering from being left partly open, so the beeping is most likely the high-temperature alarm doing its job. It is not expected to stop immediately at -9°C; it will normally clear once the compartment has cooled back towards its set temperature, often around -18°C. 1. Keep the drawer shut and avoid opening it or adding food for several hours. The number should continue falling; that suggests it is recovering normally.
2. Make sure nothing is now holding the drawer out and the seal sits flat all the way round. A continuing gap would stop it reaching temperature.
3. If there is an Alarm/Reset button, it may silence the beep, but only use it after the drawer is fully shut; the flashing temperature may remain until it has recovered. If it reaches roughly -18°C and the alarm clears, no repair is needed. If it cannot get below about -12 to -15°C after being shut for several hours, or it keeps alarming once it is properly cold, then a sealing issue, temperature sensor or cooling fault needs investigating.
there's a button with a bell icon, pressed it and the beeping stopped. is that ok to leave it then?

Yes, it is fine to leave it now. The bell button has silenced the high-temperature alarm; it does not stop the freezer cooling. With the drawer now properly shut and the displayed temperature already falling, it should continue recovering towards about -18°C. Keep the drawer shut as much as possible for the next several hours and avoid putting warm food in. The flashing temperature should stop once it is back to its normal temperature. Just make sure bags do not protrude past the drawer edge, as even a small gap can hold it open. Only investigate further if it does not get down close to -18°C after being left closed for a good while, the alarm returns with the drawer fully shut, or food starts softening again.

candidates: Door not fully closed or poor door seal triggering the door/temperature alarm (high)
Temperature alarm because the freezer is warmer than intended (medium)
Door switch, temperature sensor or control fault (low)
